Pinned.description: It's pinned in {{source}}. To uninstall it, first run {{command}} in Terminal.
Pinned.refused: It's pinned in {{source}}, so Canager didn't uninstall or change anything. Run {{command}} in Terminal to unpin it first.

NoSafeMethod.refused: Canager can't uninstall {{source}} yet. Nothing changed.

standalone-rustup.description: Rust on this Mac isn't entirely in ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup, and Canager only uninstalls Rust from those folders. rustup's documentation explains rustup self uninstall.
standalone-rustup.refused: Rust isn't entirely in ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup, so Canager didn't uninstall or change anything.

updates.neverRemindHint: You won't be reminded about any update of this again. You can undo this in Settings.

updates.selfUpdatingDetail: It usually updates itself. You can also update it now.

updates.cannotCheckSummary_other: Canager couldn't check {{count}} of these for updates. To see why, turn on “{{setting}}” in Settings.

unavailableDetail.NotRunning: {{source}} isn't running. Start it, then check again.
unavailableDetail.RefusesAsRoot: {{source}} won't run while Canager has administrator powers. Open Canager again the normal way.

Pinned.detail: It's pinned in {{source}}. To update it, first run {{command}} in Terminal.
Pinned.refused: This package has been pinned in {{source}}, so Canager didn't update it. Nothing has been changed.

SelfUpdatesOnly.detail: It updates itself: open it once and it checks for a new version.
SelfUpdatesOnly.refused: {{source}} updates itself, so Canager didn't try to update it. Nothing has been changed.

commandPreview.needsPassword: Some apps ask for your Mac password at this step.

warnings.dependentsUnknown: Couldn't check what else needs this. Make sure nothing does before you uninstall.
warnings.compilesLocally: This compiles on your Mac and takes a while.
warnings.thirdPartyRegistry: This model downloads from {{host}}, not Ollama's own library. Continue only if you trust it.

willTrash.Backups: Old copy left by an update: {{path}}

willKeep.ToolStateDetail: Some program files are in there too, so Canager keeps it whole.
willKeep.ShellConfigLinesDetail: Canager never edits this file; lines the installer added are harmless.
willKeep.OutsideHomeDetail: It's outside your home folder, so Canager leaves it. You can delete it after uninstalling.
willKeep.NotOursDetail: Canager couldn't confirm it belongs to this tool, so it stays.
willKeep.InstallerCacheDetail: It's in ~/.cache, which many tools share, so Canager leaves it. You can delete it yourself.

warnings.removesToolchains: Permanently deletes {{path}}: toolchains {{names}} and everything rustup downloaded.
warnings.removesToolchainsUnlisted: Permanently deletes {{path}}: every toolchain and everything rustup downloaded.
warnings.removesToolchainsDetail: Nothing goes to the Trash. Projects that need Rust won't build until you reinstall it.
warnings.deletesCargoHome: Permanently deletes {{path}}: Cargo's cache, settings and saved login.
warnings.deletesCargoHomeDetail: Nothing goes to the Trash, and everything else in the folder goes too.
warnings.removesCargoInstalled_one: Also permanently deletes {{names}} from the Cargo folder.
warnings.removesCargoInstalled_other: Also permanently deletes {{count}} programs from the Cargo folder: {{names}}.
warnings.removesCargoInstalledDetail: After you reinstall Rust, cargo install can put back the ones it installed.
warnings.homebrewRustupLosesToolchains: Homebrew's rustup shares these folders, so its toolchains go too.
warnings.editsShellConfig: rustup removes the line it added to your Terminal settings files.
warnings.leavesShellConfigLine: {{path}} keeps a line that loads Cargo, so a terminal that reads this file shows an error each time it starts.
warnings.leavesShellConfigLineDetail: Delete that line to fix it.
warnings.leavesShellConfigLineMaybe: {{path}} has a line that mentions Cargo, which rustup won't remove.
warnings.leavesShellConfigLineMaybeDetail: Check that line after uninstalling; if your terminal shows an error when it starts, delete it.

pipReadOnly.description: You can only view pip installs here. Install Python tools with pipx or uv to update and uninstall them here.

prefixNotWritable.description: npm keeps these in a folder your account can't change, so you can only view them. After you install Node with Homebrew, you can manage the npm packages you install with it here.

unreachable.title: {{source}} isn't responding
unreachable.description: {{source}} didn't respond, so Canager can't show what it has installed.
unreachable.descriptionWithRows: What's listed for {{source}} is from the last time it answered. Later changes aren't shown.

refusesAsRoot.title: {{source}} doesn't work while Canager runs as administrator
refusesAsRoot.description: Canager was opened as administrator this time, and {{source}} refuses to run that way. Quit, then open it again with a double-click.

notRunning.title: {{source}} isn't running
notRunning.description: Open {{source}} to see what it has and check for updates.

openOllamaFailed.notInstalled: There's no Ollama app in Applications. Download it from ollama.com, install it, then press Open Ollama again.
openOllamaFailed.notInstalledDetail: The ollama command from Homebrew doesn't include the app.
openOllamaFailed.launchFailed: macOS couldn't open Ollama. Open it yourself from Applications; if that fails too, reinstall it from ollama.com.

indexMayBeStale.title: Couldn't update Homebrew's software list
indexMayBeStale.description: Canager checked for updates against the old list. Check your connection, then try again.

indexUpdating.title: Homebrew is updating its software list
indexUpdating.description: The update list shows the last results. Canager checks again by itself when it's done.

notOnPath.title: Terminal won't find this copy of {{source}} when you type {{command}}
notOnPath.description: None of the places Terminal looks in for {{command}} leads to this copy. Open a new Terminal window first; if that doesn't help, follow its install guide.

shadowedByHomebrew.title: Typing {{command}} runs a same-named program from Homebrew first
shadowedByHomebrew.description: Canager can't tell whether that one is {{source}}. Look under Homebrew on the Installed page.

shadowedByNpm.title: Typing {{command}} runs a same-named program from npm first
shadowedByNpm.description: Canager can't tell whether that one is {{source}}. Look under npm on the Installed page.

shadowedByOther.title: Typing {{command}} runs another program with the same name first
shadowedByOther.description: Canager can't identify that program. If it's on the Unknown page, you can see where it is there.

launcherOnly.title: {{source}}'s program files are missing
launcherOnly.description: This copy of {{command}} can't run any more; Uninstall cleans it up. To keep using {{source}}, reinstall it, or drag its files back from the Trash and check again.

planRefused.sourceGone: Canager can't find the tool that manages this, so nothing started. Press Check again.
planRefused.expired: This confirmation is more than 10 minutes old, so nothing ran. Open it again and confirm.
planRefused.unknown: This confirmation is no longer valid. Close it and start again.
planRefused.invalidName: Canager can't pass “{{name}}” to {{source}}, so it stopped. Nothing changed.
planRefused.programMissing: Couldn't find {{program}}. Nothing changed. Press Check again.
planRefused.spawnFailed: {{source}} couldn't start. Nothing changed. macOS said: {{detail}}
planRefused.outputTooLarge: {{source}} returned too much output, so Canager stopped. Nothing changed.
planRefused.indexUpdating: Homebrew is updating its software list, so Canager can't check dependencies reliably now. Nothing changed. Try again in a minute or two.
planRefused.refused: Something went wrong inside Canager, so it stopped. Nothing changed.

uninstallUnsafe.outsideHome: The folder holding {{path}} leads outside your home folder, so Canager won't move it. Nothing changed.
uninstallUnsafe.sharedFolder: {{path}} is in a folder other apps share, so Canager won't move it. Nothing changed.
uninstallUnsafe.missing: {{path}} is gone, so Canager stopped. Nothing changed.
uninstallUnsafe.notOwnedByYou: {{path}} belongs to another user, so Canager won't move it. Nothing changed.
uninstallUnsafe.notWhatInstructionsExpect: {{path}} isn't what Canager expected, so it won't move it. Nothing changed.
uninstallUnsafe.notWhatInstructionsExpectDetail: It, or a folder it's in, links somewhere else, or it's the wrong kind of file or can't be read.
uninstallUnsafe.overlapsKept: Canager couldn't confirm that removing the files leaves {{path}}, which it keeps, untouched, so it didn't uninstall or change anything.

operations.noCancelHint: You can't cancel this once it starts. Keep Canager and your Mac on until it finishes.
operations.noCancelHintDetail: Stopping it partway leaves the tool unusable.

logNote.waitingForBrewUpdate: Homebrew is still downloading its latest list of software, so Canager is waiting for that to finish before it starts. This usually takes a few minutes; Canager waits up to {{minutes}}. If you'd rather not wait, press Cancel — nothing has been changed yet.
logNote.readFailedStdout: Canager couldn't read any more of this command's output ({{error}}), so its output ends here.
logNote.readFailedStderr: Canager couldn't read any more of this command's error messages ({{error}}), so they end here.
logNote.trashFailed: Couldn't move {{path}} to the Trash, so the uninstall stopped here. Your Mac gave this reason: {{error}}
logNote.outOfTime: The {{seconds}} seconds Canager allows this uninstall ran out, so it stopped before moving {{path}}. Anything it already moved is in the Trash; it hasn't touched anything else. You can uninstall again to finish the rest.
logNote.backAfterUninstall: {{path}} came back after everything on the list had gone to the Trash. Canager left it where it is.

status.waitingForBrewUpdate: waiting for Homebrew to finish updating

NeedsAttention.NotInstalledAfterInstall: Needs attention: the install reported success, but it isn't installed
NeedsAttention.StillInstalledAfterUninstall: Needs attention: the uninstall seemed to succeed, but it's still installed
NeedsAttention.GoneAfterUpgrade: Needs attention: the update reported success, but it's no longer installed
NeedsAttention.UnchangedAfterUpgrade: Needs attention: the update reported success, but it's still at the same version as before. The program didn't update it — the operation log may say why.
NeedsAttention.BackAfterUninstall: Needs attention: everything on the list went to the Trash, but part of it came back afterwards — a copy of the tool that was still running can do that. The operation log names what came back. Quit the tool, then uninstall it again if it's still listed, or move what came back to the Trash yourself.

outcome.FailedSilent: Failed. The program didn't say why — the operation log may show more.

CanagerFailed.Panicked: Failed: something went wrong inside Canager while it was doing this. Check the list to see whether anything changed.
CanagerFailed.ProgramMissing: Failed: Canager couldn't find {{program}}. It may have been removed since Canager last looked. Nothing was changed.
CanagerFailed.SpawnFailed: Failed: Canager couldn't start the program, so nothing was changed. Your Mac gave this reason: {{detail}}
CanagerFailed.HomebrewStillUpdating: Failed: Canager waited {{minutes}} minutes and Homebrew was still downloading its latest list of software, so it didn't start this. Nothing was changed. Your internet connection may be slow or interrupted — try again in a little while.
CanagerFailed.PathChanged: Failed: {{path}} changed between the preview and now (a tool that updates itself can do that), so Canager stopped and left it as it is. If anything was moved to the Trash before that, the operation log lists it. Look at the preview again.
CanagerFailed.Internal: Failed: something on Canager's side didn't add up, so it didn't start and nothing was changed. This is a problem in Canager, not on your Mac.

uninstall.title: Uninstall {{name}}?
uninstall.reissued: Nothing started, so Canager checked again.
uninstall.reissuedConfirmAgain: Nothing started, so Canager checked again. Confirm once more.
uninstall.trashPreview_one: This item goes to the Trash, where you can drag it back out.
uninstall.trashPreview_other: These {{count}} items go to the Trash, where you can drag them back out.

unknown.intro: These command-line programs are on your Mac, but Canager couldn't match them to any source it knows, so it can't tell you how they got here. Canager only lists them — it never runs or deletes anything here.

unknown.attributed_other: {{count}} more programs came from sources Canager knows and are listed under them.

stopped.TimeLimit: Canager stopped after {{seconds}} seconds, so this list may be incomplete.

refreshFailed.description_other: The last refresh couldn't finish for {{count}} sources, so what you see below may be stale.
